names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 iulie, «Sfântul Mucenic Ilarie», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος», with the rank word left off. The page's hymn and its summary verse spell the name with the rough breathing, «Ἱλάριος».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. јул ст. ст., „Св. муч. Прокл и Иларије.“ — „Св. муч.“ is the rank and the second of the two bare forenames the heading enumerates is the whole of the form; «companion of Proclus» in the display name is the corpus’s own. `foldchk.py` returns `hilary-of-poitiers`, `sr`, and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts that one other holder, so this is the second folder on the form and the heading offers nothing to break it with.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 iulie — «Sfântul Mucenic Ilarie»

attestations.note: His own page dates his death to 15 iulie — «Sfântul Mucenic Ilarie s-a sfârșit în 15 zile ale lunii iulie, a treia zi după sfârșitul Sfântului Proclu» — while the Romanian calendar keeps him with Proclus on 12 iulie. The calendar's day is the one recorded; the life's own day is set down here. Nothing on the page connects him with Hilary of Poitiers, who was a bishop and a confessor.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the Greek line pairs him with Proclus exactly as the Romanian one does. The pairing and the day settle him; the corpus keeps no other Hilary on this day. The Greek page adds the reign of Trajan, the governor Maximus, and the manner of his own death — beheading, against Proclus's arrows. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints two apolytikia: the first names both men and is taken, and the second is the common of several martyrs «Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε», printed under their name, which is taken as a common and said here to be one.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.07.2026 (12. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Прокл и Иларије.“

attestations.note: The second half of the day’s first entry; the same heading, quoted whole, stands over both rows, which is what §4 requires of an enumerated company. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. The identification is his uncle and his city: „Прокл беше стриц Иларију“, and this folder is named for that very companionship. **`dates` STAY NULL**, for the same reason as his uncle’s — „у време Трајаново“ is a reign. `types` UNTOUCHED at `martyr`. **His own act is his one line**: while Proclus was being tortured Hilary came forward to the judge and said „И ја сам хришћанин“, I am a Christian too, and he was beheaded with the sword where his uncle was crucified. **THE NAME FORM FOLDS AND THE UNCLE’S DOES NOT**, which is this entry’s one finding: „Иларије“ is already held by `hilary-of-poitiers`, so the pair’s two bare forenames out of one heading go one into a fold and one into none. No new `related` rows. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Proclu și Ilarie», Glasul 4 — the common troparion of martyrs, printed here for the two of them; the spelling «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own

english.text: Your martyrs, Lord, in their struggles received from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Your strength they overthrew their torturers and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At their prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Σταυροῦ τὴν πανοπλίαν ἱερῶς ἐνδυσάμενοι, Ἰλάριε καὶ Πρόκλε, ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἠθλήσατε, καὶ δόξης οὐρανίου κοινωνοί, ἐδείχθητε ὡς μέτοχοι Χριστοῦ, διὰ τοῦτο χαρισμάτων ταὶς δωρεαίς, πυρσεύετε τοὺς κράζοντας, δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώοαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος ἀ’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the shared page of «Άγιοι Πρόκλος και Ιλάριος», and it names them both

english.text: Having sacredly put on the full armour of the Cross, Hilary and Proclus, you contended beyond nature, and were shown sharers of heavenly glory as partakers of Christ; and so by the gifts of your graces you set alight those who cry: Glory to him who strengthened you, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτῶν, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσαντο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· σχόντες γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλον· ἔθραυσαν καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτῶν ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the second apolytikion on the shared page of the two. It is the common of several martyrs, printed under their name and naming nobody else, and is copied as the page has it

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contending received from you our God the crown of incorruption; for having your strength they brought down the tyrants, and shattered the powerless insolence of the demons. By their entreaties, Christ our God, save our souls.
